mastery_target: Identify major organ systems and describe their primary functions.

questions.prompt: Which organ system breaks food down so the body can absorb nutrients?
questions.explanation: The digestive system breaks food into smaller materials and absorbs nutrients the body can use.

questions.prompt: Which organ system moves blood, oxygen, nutrients, and wastes through the body?
questions.explanation: The circulatory system transports materials through the body using the heart, blood, and blood vessels.

questions.prompt: Which organ system brings oxygen into the body and removes carbon dioxide?
questions.explanation: The respiratory system exchanges gases, bringing oxygen into the body and removing carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: Which organ system receives information, sends signals, and helps control body responses?
questions.explanation: The nervous system uses the brain, spinal cord, and nerves to receive information and send signals that coordinate responses.

questions.prompt: Which organ system works with bones to move body parts?
questions.explanation: The muscular system is made of muscles that contract and relax to move body parts, often by pulling on bones.

questions.prompt: Which organ system supports the body, protects organs, and helps with movement?
questions.explanation: The skeletal system provides support, protects organs such as the brain and heart, and works with muscles for movement.

questions.prompt: In levels of organization, what is an organ system?

answer_choices.B: a group of similar tissues doing the same job
answer_choices.C: a group of organs working together to perform major body functions
answer_choices.D: all organisms living in an environment

questions.explanation: An organ system is made of multiple organs that work together to carry out major body functions.

questions.prompt: A model shows the stomach, small intestine, and large intestine highlighted together. Which organ system is being represented?
questions.explanation: The stomach and intestines are organs that work together in the digestive system to process food and absorb nutrients.

questions.prompt: A student observes a body model with the heart and blood vessels highlighted. What primary function should the student connect to this system?
questions.explanation: The heart and blood vessels belong to the circulatory system, which transports materials such as oxygen, nutrients, and wastes.

questions.prompt: A person breathes faster during exercise. Which organ system is most directly increasing gas exchange with the air?
questions.explanation: The respiratory system increases breathing to bring in more oxygen and remove more carbon dioxide during activity.

questions.prompt: A diagram shows the brain, spinal cord, and nerves. Which function best matches this organ system?
questions.explanation: The brain, spinal cord, and nerves are parts of the nervous system, which coordinates information and responses.

questions.prompt: A student bends an arm to pick up a backpack. Which two systems are most directly working together to create the movement?
questions.explanation: Muscles contract and pull on bones, so the muscular and skeletal systems work together to move the arm.

questions.prompt: A model highlights the skull, ribs, and backbone. Which claim is best supported by the model?

answer_choices.A: The skeletal system protects some internal organs.
answer_choices.D: The respiratory system breaks down food.

questions.explanation: The skull protects the brain, the ribs protect organs in the chest, and the backbone helps protect the spinal cord.

questions.prompt: A student sorts body parts into groups. Which group correctly shows organs that belong to the same organ system?
questions.explanation: The heart, blood vessels, and blood are parts of the circulatory system and work together to transport materials.

questions.prompt: A student claims, "The small intestine is part of the digestive system because it helps absorb nutrients from broken-down food." Which evidence best supports the claim?

answer_choices.A: The small intestine connects to organs involved in processing food.
answer_choices.B: The small intestine is protected by bones.
answer_choices.C: The small intestine sends signals to the brain.
answer_choices.D: The small intestine pumps blood to the lungs.

questions.explanation: Evidence that the small intestine connects to food-processing organs supports the idea that it belongs to the digestive system.

questions.prompt: A body model shows lungs next to many blood vessels. Why is it useful to study the respiratory and circulatory systems together?

answer_choices.A: Both systems break down food before nutrients can be absorbed.
answer_choices.B: Gas exchange in the lungs connects with blood transport through the body.
answer_choices.C: Bones must contract to move air into the lungs.
answer_choices.D: Nerves store oxygen until the body needs it.

questions.explanation: The respiratory system exchanges gases in the lungs, and the circulatory system transports those gases through the blood.

questions.prompt: A student says the heart is an organ, not an organ system. Which explanation best supports the student’s idea?

answer_choices.A: The heart is made of many organs that all do different jobs.
answer_choices.B: The heart is one structure that helps pump blood, while the circulatory system includes the heart, blood, and vessels.
answer_choices.C: The heart belongs to the respiratory system because it is near the lungs.
answer_choices.D: The heart is a tissue because it is larger than a cell.

questions.explanation: An organ is one body structure with a specific function. An organ system includes multiple organs or parts working together.

questions.prompt: A person quickly pulls a hand away from something hot. Which reasoning best explains how organ systems are involved?

answer_choices.A: The digestive system absorbs heat and the skeletal system removes it.
answer_choices.B: The nervous system detects and signals danger, while muscles move the hand.
answer_choices.C: The respiratory system pumps blood to the fingers.
answer_choices.D: The skeletal system breaks down food for energy.

questions.explanation: The nervous system helps detect the stimulus and send signals, and the muscular system produces movement to pull the hand away.

questions.prompt: A model shows ribs surrounding the lungs. Which conclusion is best supported by the model?

answer_choices.A: The skeletal system can protect organs in another organ system.
answer_choices.B: The respiratory system controls all bones in the body.
answer_choices.C: The circulatory system breaks ribs into nutrients.
answer_choices.D: The muscular system is made only of lungs.

questions.explanation: The ribs are part of the skeletal system, and their position around the lungs shows that bones can protect organs from another system.

questions.prompt: A student is comparing the muscular and skeletal systems. Which statement best explains their relationship?

answer_choices.A: The skeletal system sends signals, and the muscular system absorbs nutrients.
answer_choices.B: The muscular system pulls on bones, and the skeletal system provides structure for movement.
answer_choices.C: The muscular system pumps air, and the skeletal system removes carbon dioxide.
answer_choices.D: The skeletal system digests food, and the muscular system stores oxygen.

questions.explanation: Muscles create force by contracting, and bones provide structure and attachment points that allow body parts to move.

questions.prompt: A student uses a body model to argue that organs are grouped into systems based on shared functions. Which example best supports this argument?

answer_choices.A: The stomach and intestines are grouped because they both help process food.
answer_choices.B: The lungs and skull are grouped because they are both in the upper body.
answer_choices.C: The heart and stomach are grouped because they are both soft organs.
answer_choices.D: The ribs and nerves are grouped because they are both long structures.

questions.explanation: Organs are grouped into systems because they work together on related functions. The stomach and intestines both help process food as part of digestion.
